image_description: A medium shot of a male subject wearing academic regalia, including a black gown with wide sleeves, a blue and white hood or stole, and an orange trim. He is also wearing a mortarboard cap. The subject is raising his right hand in a wave. The background appears to be a textured wall.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped at the waist/chest level; the lower half of the garment and ankles are not visible, making full-length verification impossible.
The visible portion of the gown shows a clear vertical center line with symmetrical panels on either side, consistent with a front-opening robe.
The fabric hangs loosely around the shoulders and torso, successfully hiding the underlying body shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The sleeve on the subject's left side (viewer's right) is clearly visible as a wide, bell-shaped extension that hangs significantly past the wrist/hand area.
Distinct vertical panels are visible running down the front of the chest, characteristic of academic gown construction.
A white collared shirt is clearly visible at the neckline underneath the gown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Heavy matte fabric typically black polyester or wool blend.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The black fabric absorbs light with minimal specular reflection, indicating a matte, heavy weave typical of academic robes.
The texture appears uniform and smooth without high-gloss highlights.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Characteristic sleeve drape extending past the wrist.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by the visible drape of the sleeve on the viewer's right, which extends well beyond the natural arm length.

The brick/stone pattern in the background has a slightly smeared, painterly quality inconsistent with optical focus, suggesting minor generative smoothing.

alignment_reasoning: The image demonstrates excellent class conformance for 'academic gown'. All testable checkpoints regarding silhouette, sleeve structure, material properties, and layering are met perfectly. The only untestable checkpoint is the full length due to cropping, but the visible evidence strongly supports the classification.

The fingers are malformed and fused, a common AI generation failure mode for hands. This significantly impacts the overall artifact score despite the high quality of the primary subject (the gown).
